reason: The cited evidence (E1, E3) directly shows that rapid quenching produces an amorphous structure and slow cooling produces crystalline phases, supporting the first two premises. It also states that phosphorus enhances glass-forming ability, supporting the third. However, the evidence does not provide any data on the thermal stability (e.g., crystallization temperatures) of the amorphous state relative to the slow-cooled baseline, nor does it discuss kinetic trapping or improved short-range ordering; these key premises are unsupported.
premises: Rapid quenching (10^5–10^6 K/s) of Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 yields an amorphous structure
Slow cooling (52 K/s) of the same alloy yields a complex crystalline microstructure
Phosphorus addition enhances glass-forming ability during rapid cooling
Higher cooling rate suppresses crystallization via kinetic trapping
The amorphous state from rapid cooling exhibits higher thermal stability (e.g., higher crystallization onset temperature) than the slow-cooled state
